<details>
<summary>🔒 Does your organisation require pull requests on <code>main</code>?</summary><br/>

If pushing to `main` is rejected (`GH013: Repository rule violations found … Changes must be made through a pull request`), push your work to a branch instead. Wherever the exercise says "commit and push":

**Command line**

```bash
git add -A && git commit -m "My solution"
git push origin HEAD:my-solution    # use this same line for every push
```

**GitHub Desktop**

1. Once: click **Current Branch** at the top, then **New Branch**. Name it `my-solution` and click **Create Branch**. Check that `my-solution` is now the current branch.
2. In the **Changes** tab, write a short summary (for example "My solution") and click **Commit to my-solution**.
3. Click **Publish branch** the first time, or **Push origin** on later pushes.

The check runs on every push to your branch, and I'll post the result here in this issue.

**On GitHub (optional): get your work onto `main`**

You don't need this to complete the exercise. If you want your changes on `main`, open your repository on GitHub, click **Compare & pull request** on the yellow banner (or go to the **Pull requests** tab → **New pull request**, pick `my-solution`), then **Create pull request** and **Merge pull request**. In GitHub Desktop, **Branch → Create Pull Request** takes you to the same page.

Don't worry if the README on `main` still shows the start text. Your steps and progress are in this issue.

</details>
